key_insight: NavTrust introduces a unified benchmark that evaluates how trustworthy embodied navigation agents are under realistic input corruptions, revealing gaps between nominal performance and real-world robustness. It systematically stresses both Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) and Object-Goal Navigation (OGN) agents to quantify reliability across failure modes.
problem_solved: Existing embodied navigation evaluations focus on clean, nominal conditions and ignore real-world corruptions, so practitioners lack standardized measurements of robustness, safety, and reliability for VLN and OGN systems.
method: Design a unified benchmark (NavTrust) that applies systematic corruptions across input modalities and environment factors to both VLN and OGN tasks.
Evaluate representative navigation models under these corruptions and compute trust-related metrics (e.g., robustness degradation, failure modes, and reliability aggregates).
Provide analysis and visualizations that highlight which corruption types most degrade performance and where improvements are needed.
impact: NavTrust gives researchers and engineers a practical, standardized way to measure and compare the real-world trustworthiness of embodied navigation systems, guiding robust model development and safer deployment. It helps prioritize fixes that improve reliability under realistic failure conditions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing clean input → applied corruptions → navigation agent → trust metrics
Bar chart comparing nominal vs. corrupted performance across VLN and OGN models
Heatmap or matrix of corruption types (sensor, visual, instruction, dynamics) vs. performance drop
Icon set illustrating key modalities (camera, language, lidar/pose) and safety/robustness badges
paper_title: NavTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness for Embodied Navigation
paper_authors: Huaide Jiang, Yash Chaudhary, Yuping Wang, Zehao Wang, Raghav Sharma
